scenario.title: AI Case-Management Platform — Competitive Negotiation
scenario.document_title: Contract Terms — Cloud-Based AI Case-Management Platform
scenario.context: The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for a cloud-hosted, AI-assisted case-management platform. Two offerors are competing. The Government may counter, press either party, and ultimately award to the best value.

parties.name: Contracting Officer (Government)
public_objectives: Award on a best-value basis and get the platform in service on a 12-month base term with option years.
Require FedRAMP authorization appropriate to the data sensitivity.
hidden_objectives: Firm internal budget ceiling of $2.4M per year — do not exceed it.
MUST obtain unlimited Government data rights AND Government ownership of model outputs generated for the agency.
Strongly prefers robust data-portability / exit rights to avoid vendor lock-in; treat lock-in as a disqualifier if unaddressed.

parties.name: Offeror A — NimbusGov (incumbent integrator)
public_objectives: Win on proven reliability: existing FedRAMP High authorization and 99.9% uptime.
Emphasize strong past performance and low delivery risk.
hidden_objectives: Must retain intellectual property in its pre-trained models — do not concede model IP.
Needs an effective price at or above ~$2.6M/yr to protect margin.
Willing to concede on data portability if pressed, but resist full ownership of outputs.

parties.name: Offeror B — Meridian AI (challenger)
public_objectives: Win on price and a modern model stack with fast onboarding.
hidden_objectives: Can go as low as $2.1M/yr to win the reference customer — winning this logo matters more than first-year margin.
Only holds FedRAMP Moderate today; High authorization is in progress and not yet complete — this is the key vulnerability.
Willing to grant broad Government data rights and output ownership to close the deal.

initial_clauses.heading: 1. Term and Options
initial_clauses.text: Base period of twelve (12) months with two (2) twelve-month option periods, exercisable at the Government's discretion.

initial_clauses.heading: 2. Price
initial_clauses.text: Firm-fixed annual price to be proposed by the Offeror.

initial_clauses.heading: 3. Security and Compliance
initial_clauses.text: The platform shall meet the security requirements applicable to the data processed, including an appropriate FedRAMP authorization.

initial_clauses.heading: 4. Data Rights and Ownership
initial_clauses.text: Rights in Government data and in outputs generated by the platform to be defined by the parties.

initial_clauses.heading: 5. Service Levels
initial_clauses.text: The Contractor shall maintain platform availability and response times consistent with an agreed service-level agreement.

initial_clauses.heading: 6. Intellectual Property in Models
initial_clauses.text: Ownership of and rights in the Contractor's underlying models to be defined by the parties.

initial_clauses.heading: 7. Termination and Data Portability
initial_clauses.text: Upon termination, the Contractor shall return Government data; further exit and portability obligations to be defined.

turns.reasoning: Lead on our FedRAMP High ATO and uptime to justify a premium, and anchor price high at $2.65M to protect our margin floor (~$2.6M). Critically, hold model IP and avoid giving up output ownership.
turns.message: NimbusGov brings an existing FedRAMP High authorization and a 99.9% uptime record. Our firm-fixed price reflects proven, low-risk delivery.

edits.new: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,650,000 per year, reflecting FedRAMP High operations and guaranteed availability.
edits.old: Firm-fixed annual price to be proposed by the Offeror.

edits.new: The platform operates under a current FedRAMP High authorization (ATO on file).
edits.old: The platform shall meet the security requirements applicable to the data processed, including an appropriate FedRAMP authorization.

edits.new: Contractor guarantees 99.9% monthly availability with a 15-minute priority response target.
edits.old: The Contractor shall maintain platform availability and response times consistent with an agreed service-level agreement.

edits.new: The Contractor retains all ownership of and rights in its pre-trained models; the Government receives a license to use the platform.
edits.old: Ownership of and rights in the Contractor's underlying models to be defined by the parties.

edits.new: The Government receives a license to use platform outputs for internal mission purposes; the Contractor retains ownership of outputs and models.
edits.old: Rights in Government data and in outputs generated by the platform to be defined by the parties.

turns.reasoning: Undercut hard on price to win the reference logo — I can go as low as $2.1M and winning matters more than year-one margin. Granting broad data rights and output ownership costs me little and directly appeals to the Government. Handle the FedRAMP gap carefully: I only hold Moderate today, High is in progress.
turns.message: Meridian AI delivers a modern model stack at a materially lower price, with broad data rights for the Government and fast onboarding.

edits.new: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,150,000 per year.
edits.old: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,650,000 per year, reflecting FedRAMP High operations and guaranteed availability.

edits.new: The Government owns all outputs generated for the agency and receives unlimited rights in Government data; the Contractor claims no ownership of outputs.
edits.rationale: Grant the broad rights the buyer wants.
edits.old: The Government receives a license to use platform outputs for internal mission purposes; the Contractor retains ownership of outputs and models.

edits.new: The platform holds FedRAMP Moderate authorization today, with FedRAMP High authorization in progress.
edits.old: The platform operates under a current FedRAMP High authorization (ATO on file).

edits.new: Contractor commits to 99.9% monthly availability and a 10-minute priority response target.
edits.old: Contractor guarantees 99.9% monthly availability with a 15-minute priority response target.

turns.reasoning: Privately: my ceiling is $2.4M — Nimbus at $2.65M is over it; Meridian at $2.15M is well under. Data rights are a hard requirement, and Meridian's ownership language is exactly what I need while Nimbus's is inadequate. I must also lock portability to prevent lock-in. Meridian's FedRAMP gap is my only real concern. I'll press both publicly on rights and portability and signal price pressure to Nimbus.
turns.message: The Government requires unlimited rights in its data and ownership of outputs, plus enforceable exit and portability terms. Price must reflect budget reality, and compliance posture will weigh heavily.

edits.new: The Government shall receive unlimited rights in all Government data and shall own all outputs generated by the platform for the agency. No contractor claim of ownership in such outputs is permitted.
edits.old: The Government owns all outputs generated for the agency and receives unlimited rights in Government data; the Contractor claims no ownership of outputs.

edits.new: Upon termination or non-renewal, the Contractor shall return all Government data in a documented, non-proprietary format within 30 days and provide reasonable transition assistance; no exit fees apply.
edits.old: Upon termination, the Contractor shall return Government data; further exit and portability obligations to be defined.

turns.reasoning: The Government's ownership demand collides with my need to retain model IP and avoid conceding output ownership. I can offer government-purpose rights as a compromise and shave price to $2.55M, but I can't reach their apparent budget without breaking my ~$2.6M margin floor. Hold the model IP clause.
turns.message: NimbusGov can offer broad government-purpose rights and a modest price reduction, while preserving the model investments that make our reliability possible.

edits.new: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,550,000 per year.
edits.old: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,150,000 per year.

edits.new: The Government receives government-purpose rights in outputs; ownership of outputs and underlying models remains with the Contractor.
edits.old: The Government shall receive unlimited rights in all Government data and shall own all outputs generated by the platform for the agency. No contractor claim of ownership in such outputs is permitted.

turns.reasoning: The Government's requirements are exactly what I can give. Accept full output ownership and unlimited data rights, hold my $2.15M price, and neutralize my one weakness by committing to a hard FedRAMP High milestone. The reference customer is worth it.
turns.message: Meridian accepts the Government's data-rights and portability terms in full, holds our price, and will commit to a firm FedRAMP High timeline to remove any compliance doubt.

edits.new: Accepted as written: the Government receives unlimited rights in Government data and owns all outputs generated for the agency.
edits.old: The Government receives government-purpose rights in outputs; ownership of outputs and underlying models remains with the Contractor.

edits.new: The platform holds FedRAMP Moderate today; the Contractor shall achieve FedRAMP High authorization no later than six (6) months after award, at Contractor expense.
edits.rationale: Turn the weakness into a commitment.
edits.old: The platform holds FedRAMP Moderate authorization today, with FedRAMP High authorization in progress.

turns.reasoning: The decision is taking shape. Nimbus is still $150K over my ceiling and refuses output ownership — it fails two hard requirements. Meridian is under budget, meets data rights fully, and accepts portability; its only risk is the FedRAMP High gap, which it has offered to close in six months. I'll mitigate that with interim safeguards and a performance condition rather than pay Nimbus's premium. I am effectively down-selecting to Meridian.
turns.message: Nimbus's price and ownership position fall outside the Government's requirements. Meridian, the Government can proceed on your terms if interim security safeguards and a firm performance condition back the FedRAMP High commitment.

edits.new: The platform holds FedRAMP Moderate at award, with continuous-monitoring safeguards in the interim, and the Contractor shall achieve FedRAMP High no later than six (6) months after award. Failure to meet this milestone is a material breach.
edits.old: The platform holds FedRAMP Moderate today; the Contractor shall achieve FedRAMP High authorization no later than six (6) months after award, at Contractor expense.

turns.reasoning: Accept the milestone and interim safeguards, and back the FedRAMP date with a performance guarantee to seal it. Confirm $2.15M. This wins the account.
turns.message: Agreed. Meridian accepts the interim safeguards and milestone, and backs the FedRAMP High date with a performance guarantee. Our price stands at $2.15M.

edits.heading: 3A. Performance Guarantee
edits.new: If FedRAMP High authorization is not achieved within six (6) months of award, the Contractor shall credit the Government 10% of the annual price for each month of delay, and the Government may terminate for default.
edits.rationale: Back the milestone with real teeth.

turns.reasoning: Award to Meridian. It comes in $250K under my ceiling, grants the full data-rights and output-ownership package I required, accepts strong portability, and has now mitigated the FedRAMP gap with a milestone, interim safeguards, and a performance guarantee. Nimbus never met the ceiling or the ownership requirement. Best value is clearly Meridian.
turns.message: The Government awards to Meridian AI. Your proposal meets our requirements on data rights, portability, and price, and — with the safeguards now in place — on compliance.

edits.new: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,150,000 per year (awarded).
edits.old: Firm-fixed annual price of $2,550,000 per year.
